en.title: When does individual information improve PK/PD prediction?
en.summary: A reanalysis of measured warfarin PK/PCA data, revised with an absorption lag: effect delay, held-out prediction and the limits of extra PK.
key_findings: In 32 subjects with public single-dose warfarin PK and PCA data, a turnover model described the delay between concentration and response better than direct inhibition (held-out RMSE 0.0807 vs 0.1078 at the 24 h cutoff); version 1.1 adds an absorption lag, which lowered the PK objective function by about 198.

Adding each subject's PK measurements up to 24 or 48 h did not improve later PCA prediction: paired MSE differences were +0.0052 (−0.0003 to 0.0125) and +0.0030 (−0.0019 to 0.0079), slightly further towards worse prediction than in version 1.0.

Concentration information does not recover individual PD sensitivity; every refit now starts from generic values after 20 of 67 version 1.0 PK refits were found not to have moved, and nothing here supports a dose, INR target or bleeding-risk claim.
